summary: FlameIQ is an interactive, SI-powered dashboard that turns NASA’s microgravity fire experiments into fire safety insights for human space exploration. Decades of results are scattered across technical reports, so they are hard to find, compare and apply. FlameIQ summarizes each experiment in plain language, ranks the evidence by how closely it matches a chosen mission scenario (ISS-like, Moon, Mars or deep-space cabin), and uses SI to answer questions with cited experiment IDs. A 3D mission lab shows how gravity, oxygen and airflow change flame behavior, and a coverage map reveals where no test exists, such as partial gravity. It matters because crews returning to the Moon and travelling to Mars will breathe different cabin air, and fire is one of the most dangerous hazards in a spacecraft.
details:
What it does: FlameIQ catalogues 10 NASA microgravity fire experiments (Saffire-I to VI and ISS flame-quenching tests) with their oxygen level, pressure, airflow, flame size and spread rate. Users choose a scenario or set oxygen, pressure and gravity, and the dashboard ranks the experiments by relevance, hazard and evidence quality. The weights are adjustable and the scoring is transparent math, not a black box.

How it works: records transcribed from NASA reports feed the ranking engine. An SI layer (a Claude model) answers questions using only those records, cites experiment IDs, quotes numbers exactly, and flags thin evidence. A scenario briefing shows oxygen partial pressure compared with sea-level air, the best-matching experiment, and a confidence rating.

Features: a coverage map of tested conditions; figures for flame size, spread rate, CO₂ released and the oxygen trend across Saffire flights; and a 3D lab with a Moon, Mars, Earth and orbit globe plus a flame view that responds to gravity, oxygen and airflow.

Benefits and impact: planners find relevant evidence in seconds, see where data is missing, and can trace every claim to a source. Our catalogue has no partial-gravity records, so FlameIQ flags Moon and Mars scenarios as low confidence instead of guessing.

Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, inline SVG and HTML canvas for the figures and 3D scenes, and a Claude model for Q&A.

Creativity: combining ranking, SI interpretation, gap detection and an interactive 3D view in one dashboard. The 3D flame is a stylized illustration, not a combustion simulation.

SI acknowledgement: the page code was written with SI assistance (Claude), and the Q&A feature uses a Claude model. The planet and flame visuals are drawn by code, not SI-generated images. This is also stated in the page footer and metadata.
